# `Net`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Net — typed network primitives.

`Port` is an opaque TCP/UDP port number.  The ONLY way to build one is
`fromInt`, which REJECTS any value outside the valid `1..65535` range (0 is
the reserved "no port" sentinel and is not a dialable port, so it is
rejected too).  Because a `Port` is validated at construction, every
connection surface that used to take a bare `Int` — `Email.SmtpConfig.port`,
`Db.Dsn.build` — now takes a `Port`, so an out-of-range or zero port is a
construction-time `Err`, never a value that reaches a live socket.

Recover the raw number at the runtime boundary with `toInt`.

## `Port`

An opaque, range-validated TCP/UDP port.  Construct only via `fromInt`.
The constructor is NOT exported, so a `Port` is a proof that its wrapped
value is in `1..65535`.

## `fromInt`

```ipe
fromInt : Int -> Result Error Port
```

`fromInt n` — the parse-don't-validate seal: the only `Port` constructor.
Returns `Ok` when `n` is in `1..65535`, otherwise `Err` (a port of 0, a
negative, or a value above 65535 is not a dialable port).

## `toInt`

```ipe
toInt : Port -> Int
```

`toInt port` — recover the raw port number for the runtime boundary.

## `min`

```ipe
min : Port
```

The smallest valid port (`1`).  A total value — useful as the seed for
`Result.withDefault` when a compile-time-known-valid literal (e.g. a default
config port) is built through `fromInt`.

## `max`

```ipe
max : Port
```

The largest valid port (`65535`).  A total value.
